workstream: split the two registration-key rules so they stop competing

split.registrationKeys: settings built in the same method as Registry.register (it can see the id)
split.registry-key-context: settings built inside a lambda, where the id lives on the wrapper's stack (ResourcefulLib path)

mechanism.constructorRedirects.skipWhenCallsOwner/: the context rule declines any method that calls Registry.register
mechanism.insertBeforeCalls.onlyInClass/onlyInMeth: the supplier rule is scoped to FabricRegistryEntry.of

unscopedSupplierRule.consequence: the other 31 would emit getWithKey(Supplier, class_2378, class_2960) while locals 0/1 hold other types - verification failure

lesson: an insert rule must be scoped: its arguments come from local slots, and the same callee elsewhere has a different layout. 32 firings looked like good coverage and was 31 latent verification failures.
notYet: the scope descriptor is copied from javap; a ResourcefulLib update would make the rule fire 0 times (silent no-op, not a wrong edit)
